text:
Dashing in, ungainly and semi-lucid.

	It didn’t have to show it’s face to me, but I remember that it did, briefly.

	It was pockmarked, red, and inflamed.

	I had never seen it that way before.

	We didn’t really meet eye-to-eye, there was too much distraction. I had company, and it struggled to hold its own against the racing in-between. Our glances were furtive but not intimate.

	And the crickets, so many crickets.

	It pretended not to love me the same way I pretended to love it; compulsory and third-hearted.

	The lunar eclipse.


It must have felt hurt, for the next night it shone so full and bright and in such a cloudless sky my shadow was lighter than me. Again that impersonal grace of the disinterested and honor-bound, quietly embarrassed by unrequited vulnerability.

	It no longer looked at me, though I at it, pleadingly.

	I had wronged it more than I knew, I gathered.

	I was left in the care and attention of the land, shown to me as it was only through the silvery pallor in the air.

	Maybe it cannot help but love.

I see your jewels and ask whether you want them,

	overburdened with weight noone has plucked,

	now finally drawing bites from

	just the decomposers.

	Overgrown bells of color and scent,

	pealing thickly,

	striker cloying to the lip.

	Your gifts are all streaked with brown,

	that overdue attention coming now from

	the hours caulked to your body.

	You are caught in the dripping weight

	of your hopeful youth;

	flamboyant, embarrassed, tired,

	insulated by detritus

	and chalky wet sweetcoat.

	At least you are in the good company

	of the large and dangling decay.

	Your heavy limbs,

	limp with opulence,

	press the ground

	side by side with the overperfumed excess

	of those who could not control themselves.

AND SO, IS IT OVER?

	a question hung over the summerflowers. what could they know? that the answer was “yes”? the machine still huddled on the sidelines, shy, almost dainty. the buds wobbled up on thin wiry stems, swaying for the sun. How could they know it would tear them? with the birds hopping about looking for worms; and the worms themselves wriggling below. how could they know it was already over?

	only after being overwhelmed. all those whiteyellow heads, popping over the grass. only after the lashed beast screamed its wakeup, and showed itself to quake not from fear but from power. and moving, too; it was live, and it was diligent. as a process of time, every flower was impressed; first by sound, then by deafening sight, then by a whirlwind totality for just a dark instant.

	as it destroyed the world, the birds took flight and the worms burrowed. but you would be proud; not a single bloom yielded. all stayed put, as proud and tall always as they were when born. you would think they didn’t notice their halved sisters and cousins.

	ah, well. a message was passed continually on, always moments away from metal. “NO”; shouted over and over by every flower, for every other. the screeching bulk as seen by a thousand eyes, pressing and furious, chased the call. their answer and realization; no, it was not over. a terror was not the end, and neither was the morning. a new question would hang; how beautiful the next surge of life would be?

	and how beautiful they are now, that their faceless stalks stand brave and still?

I have never broken cleanly;

	greenstick fractured relations.

Bugs kept getting into my room, so I taped up the gaps in my windows with plastic tarp. Now I hear them breathing, always. The fabric is sucked in, pushed out, and sucked back in again constantly with the changing air pressure. It comforts me to hear nature’s steady breath. At night they move shallowly. The world breathes at such a different rate than humans, yet there is still the telltale tranquility or rapid inhales that come with caprice. It is windy today; they hyperventilate in unsteady bursts.

Finally; my favorite thing again.

	Can probably catch the moon

	in the morning.

i make a painting that always makes you feel the exact same whenever you look at it. I show you and you never look away and die gazing at it. You are never done looking at it because you always have the exact same feeling while seeing it, so your mind never moves on. The Stunlock Portrait.

Humans are adrenaline seekers and experiencers, and we know that about ourselves. Hundreds swarm to Pulpit Rock daily to see what it’s like standing on that huge huge outcropping. How dangerous! What could happen! Look at this! We all gather around and pray to the safety beneath our feet because it feels better to pray for something that may be taken away than to pray for something you have forever.

Samsara, reincarnation, etc; where the more advanced forms of life are the bugs and bacteria, rather than humans. Living good lives gets you reincarnated into lower and lower forms of life. Eventually, to escape samara, you get to be reborn as the inanimate.
You can feel what it's doing to you. You woke up and your hands were shaking; you felt that. You were not lying to yourself when your unsteady legs gave out under you.

Late winter/early spring rain feels like the season allowing itself to cry. It has understood that it is not being watched, it understands how it has been hurting, and it cries for itself. Sobbing with self-humility, head up again, feeling the tight grip of grief finally loosen.

	petulant and proud. As the busy world is hoping for a quick transition to sun and leaves, the season insists upon its own time, its own slow transition. Nature must process before it can move on. Refusing to be rushed, and perfectly gradual. There is no instant sun; there is a prolonged inbetween of silence and still. There has never been an instant sun.

	A period of time unmemorable in event, and often forgotten, but no less complete and proud of its own existence while it lives. A noble pride in its transitionary but full life.

	Unresponsive to expectations from others, and pure. Like observing someone, without their knowing, after their weeping but before they have dried their tears. When everything feels curiously open, before the need to clean up and fill the empty space encroaches; misty blank light, detritus, and the flitting watchful soul.

	When the buds have appeared on trees, but before they have opened. What patience they have, to wait and wait! Day after overcast day, knowing the sun will come soon, but no desire to rush to it. Everything waiting in anticipation of vibrant warmth, but so content with waiting - so caught up in motionless observance of the others around them - as to feel that it will never come. No excitement or fear for the coming rays, just knowledge of their approach. Unafraid to rain with confidence.

	…

	so assured of the coming sun that they are unafraid to lose it. Glad, in fact, that it is not here yet. There is a certain wonder after a harsh winter, not at the presence of the warm sun but at the lack of the bitter cold. The empty adjustment period, when the absence of what was just oppressing the whole world is so complete that it blocks out any thought. Not through overpowering the mind, or overpowering the landscape; exactly the opposite. Space for the first time; a full breath, for the first time. Not of clear air, but of clearer air. The intuitive, innate knowledge that it will only get clearer. When you feel like glass, fragile and empty and seethrough, and it is all you can do to exist patiently. All the grass and bark can do is wait. And so they wait.
The frog is scared, and can’t move its legs. It begins to sink. It manages to croak “Why? Won’t you drown too?” with a look backward. It sees the scorpion is crying.
Infested with something that wont stop making my skin bubble and twitch in response to my own thoughts.

They couldn't catch me, the ghost of it all.

	I heard them whispering, trying to find me.

	They guessed a glittery version of me into being -

	an echo of me, afraid of me,

	looking right at me.

	I don't think they realized.

	No way to rest except to lay my hands on myself;

	not after that injustice.

	So I kissed the apparition, and below us

	the conspirators startled, grew sheepish,

	and after that even I was gone.

Waiting to see what emotions will come, and

	high off the idea that I could, ever, once, have enough to eat

I refuse to believe poetry cannot be found in dopamine dumpstercore technological adlands. Starting a quest to regain it. Goodbye poetry of quiet, peace, nature and plants; hello poetry of mental bodies grinding against each other, of souls compression-scraped against the raw hides of religion, cenotaph, and opinion.
Oh tree, you've lost your leaves so fast. Does it hurt you to have them? Is that why you don't keep them?
With whose eyes are you seeing this world, and with whose mouth are you making these claims?
I'm not the one choosing to remember this

Born into this beating body. Let me say this; I am scared of every pulse. I do not know what is happening under my skin. I only know that should it stop, I will be different for a short period of time, and then I will die.

Summersun I cannot face you. You are full of smoghorn and your signature increasing hothaze. You are radioactive and I am warned by everyone, including my own instinct, to stay away. I can only face you, summer, during the nights. I can only come out when you are asleep and unaware and will not bite me for inspecting your form over the landscape. You make me treat you like a beast.
I see myself often as a thing not far from the dirt scrabbling around, maintaining fear, and acting coy for nobody but itself.

This is the human form; it’s all you are. Flashes of bodies, flashes of necks. Look at your hands, they’re just like these ones. There is no default human hand; the hands we just showed you are just one person’s. We are all modeled the same, do you think your legs are the same as hers? You love to think about yourself, so think about yourself. Picture the body. Your existence is known through it. Stories are told through it. We understand the world by using human bodies as the playing pieces. All complex emotions borne only from connection to the human form. Consider how you know the body. How many different bodies you’ve seen. How many different ways you’ve been told a body looks. Physical. Photographs. Drawings. Symbols. Stylized characters. Videos. All of humans. Human being bodies. You cannot help but want to look at them. Why else do you fret so? On your phone? Out in public? You want to see more people. You want to see more humans. Bodies. Hear them talk, in languages you recognize. See them do what you have done. See them face your same challenges. Humans to humans for humans.

I want to unroll myself in public. I want to be crucified in front of a large crowd. I want to be found when I least expect but most want to be found and hear noises of affection and pity from my observer. I want my name said again and again. I want people to not be able to take their eyes off me, I want them to cry or scream or stare silent. I want my name said louder. If the clouds shake and disperse from the sonic force of my essence it won’t be enough. I want my idealized self before everyone’s eyes. I want people to wonder what they should take from me, and then I want them to take it, and I want to become a piece smaller. I want to wither just so I can be the object of someone’s wish to water. I want people to think of me shallowly but constantly. Is that it? I want to be high flung on a lifted platform, and on the platform I want to be bleeding and twisted and I want my skin to be stretched out and pinned down. I want cameras pointed down at my body, and I want it broadcast, and I want to hear the city sigh and shake with emotional intensity beneath me. I want to compel without a movement, I want my inaction to form a gleaming chrysalis around me, I want to be more special than you. I want my name said louder.
If you can’t think of anything you haven’t ever thought about, call me

My drunken mind strayed on the fitful edge a moment too long, and I passed to waking in some circumstance around 6:00 in the morning. Dim, soggy, ink-stamp impressions of experiences whirled past me. It was a somber awakening, and I felt so weak. I had not eaten enough - my body was more tired than it had been in a while, and I felt the sort of pull to sleep like maggots decomposing me, my body fearful of activity and clinging to stillness as long as it could. My eyes opened anyway, and found my room colored. Pure orange, with fringes tinged green. It felt like looking at a mother’s face. With great willpower, I raised my head and turned it to the window. I now heard, dimly, with my ear off the pillow, a rumbling sound. I was under an active thunderstorm, and the air was charged with ozone. Through a scratchy black haze of exhaustion i saw, brilliant and streaked with whitelight, the sun off a million leaves. They shone warmly but peeling, and my room was filled with them. My head sank, and a purpledark hood clung to my head.
The moon looks right over our heads. Just like us, it cannot help but watch the sun.
Does not the world, forever and always in everything it says, now also speak my name?
